narrative:
The model estimates an 81% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most shaped this outlook were your total years of experience, the other job offers you have received, and the sector you work in. Your relatively short overall experience of 1-5 years—shared by about half of employees predicted to stay—still pushed the prediction toward leaving. The model sees shorter career tenure as a common signal that someone may be exploring new opportunities. Receiving other job offers was the strongest factor pulling the prediction upward; having concrete alternatives outside the company strongly signals higher risk of departure. Finally, working in the “other” sector, which is less common among those expected to stay, added further weight toward leaving.

Taken together, these elements outweighed positive signals such as your medical insurance, recognition you receive, and manageable commute. Because the model cannot ignore the combination of limited tenure, external opportunities, and sector norms, it concluded you are likely to move on.

Your organization should discuss retention measures with you—such as clearer promotion paths or expanded responsibilities—while you may want to reflect on whether the external offers better match your longer-term goals. Addressing these points openly could still change the outlook.
